description: Schiffer's variational method for schlicht functions provides necessary conditions for extremal maps in the Bloch constant problem. First and second variations yield differential equations constraining extremal geometry.
mathematical_formalization: Schiffer variation: f_*(z) = f(z) + epsilon * e^{2i*theta} * f(z)^2/(f(z)-w_0) * 1/(z*f'(z)) + O(epsilon^2). Extremality condition: delta B_f = 0.
analogical_connections: Schiffer variation ~ epsilon-net in learning theory
Schlicht class constraint ~ feasibility in convex optimization
implementation_hypothesis: Numerically implement Schiffer variations. Check vanishing of first variation at candidate extremals. Iterate to converge to extremal functions.
experiment_seed: Start with Koebe function, apply variations, follow steepest ascent. Track convergence of B_f.
